  For the Regular Meeting of: May 20, 2025
Senior Planner:  Planning Manager:

SUBJECT: ZONE CHANGE FROM IF TO M3 FOR A PORTION OF THE PROPERTY
LOCATED AT 9313 RAYO AVENUE AND FINDING THAT THIS IS NOT SUBJECT TO
THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (PL25-146)

PROJECT PROPOSAL/REQUEST: Request to change the zoning designation of a portion of
the property at 9313 Rayo Avenue from IF (Industrial Flex) to M3 (Heavy Manufacturing), to
match the current M3 zoning designation of the remainder of the property. The property is located
within the Rayo Industrial (Sub-area 2) District as shown in the Community Design Element of
the General Plan. The property currently has a split-zone with the front portion designated M3 and
the rear portion designated IF. The purpose of the request is to eliminate the split-zone condition
and consolidate the entire property to M3.

BACKGROUND:

Project Overview

•  General Plan Designation: Rayo Industrial District (Sub-area 2)

•  Zoning: Industrial Flex (IF) and Heavy Manufacturing (M3)

•  Project Location: 9313 Rayo Avenue

•  Assessor’s Parcel Numbers: 6222-005-028 & 6222-005-030

•  Site Characteristics: The subject site measures approximately 99,856 square feet (2.29 acres)
  and is comprised of one irregular-shaped parcel having primary frontage along Rayo Avenue.
  A metal building remains on the southwest portion of the site, along with a storage area,
  restrooms, and other spaces inside the building. The natural grade slopes towards the
  southeastern portion of the site. Currently, a large portion of the site is paved with asphalt, with
  some concrete areas appearing to be remnants of demolished structures. There is an
  approximately 10-foot-tall solid metal fence that spans along the easterly frontage of the site.
  The site is accessible from three existing driveway aprons along its primary frontage.

  9

(Zone Change PL25-146) – 9313 Rayo Ave.
May 20, 2025
Page 2 of 4

•  Surroundings: Surrounding properties include commercial and industrial uses to the north, east
  and west, and a Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) facility to the south. A surface
  level parking lot is currently being developed directly to the north and west of the subject site
  and is intended for an Amazon parcel delivery vehicle operation. A metal recycling facility
  (ELG Metals West Coast Inc.) is located to the east across Rayo Avenue. LAUSD operates a
  maintenance yard, administrative office, and adult school to the south.

•  Project Description: The project consists of an Ordinance, amending the citywide Zoning Map
  of Title 11 (Zoning) of the SGMC, to change the zoning designation of the rear portion of the
  property at 9313 Rayo Avenue from IF (Industrial Flex) to M3 (Heavy Manufacturing), to
  match the current M3 zoning designation of the front portion of the property. The property is
  located within the Rayo Industrial (Sub-area 2) District as shown in the Community Design
  Element of the General Plan. The project does not include site or tenant improvements.

•  Applicant: Tom Wong (Commercial Development Resources Inc.), on behalf of Mr. C’s
  Towing of South Gate, Inc / FUBAR Properties LLC.

•  Municipal Code Requirements for a Zone Change: Pursuant to Table 11.50-1 (Initiation of
  Amendments) of SGMC Chapter 11.50.050(B), the City Council, Planning Commission, or
  Applicant may initiate a Zoning Map Amendment. In this project, the proposed zone change
  was requested by the Applicant.

  Furthermore, pursuant to SGMC Chapter 11.51.030, Table 11.51-1 (Application and Review
  Authority), the proposed zone change must first be reviewed at a scheduled public hearing
  before the Planning Commission. Following the hearing, the Planning Commission shall adopt
  a Resolution recommending to the City Council approval or denial. The City Council shall
  then conduct its own public hearing to consider the recommendation. If the amendment is
  approved, the City Council must adopt an Ordinance to finalize the zone change.

History of Land Use and Zoning of Subject Property

From 1941 to 1992, the site was occupied by the Cooper Drum Company, which reconditioned
steel drums containing industrial chemicals. The property remained vacant for many years due to
contamination and has been deemed a Superfund site by the United States Environmental
Protection Agency (EPA). Throughout the years, the site has been partially treated with the
installation of test wells and extraction of some chemicals. EPA has continued to oversee cleanup
operations conducted by the prior and current property owners. Due to the site’s contamination,
EPA imposed certain limitations in conducting site improvements and type of land uses/activities
permitted within the site. The EPA restrictions in combination with the City’s Zoning Code have
limited the uses/activities and improvements that may be permitted within the subject site.

In 2013, the property lot lines were adjusted to create the current lot configuration consisting of
two Assessor parcel numbers. Although it consists of two parcel numbers, the site is identified as
one legal parcel. At the time, the entire property’s zoning designation was “M2” (light

  10
 Planning Commission
(Zone Change PL25-146) – 9313 Rayo Ave.
May 20, 2025
Page 3 of 4

manufacturing). Subsequently, the Zoning Code was comprehensively updated in 2015, which
resulted in amendments to the Zoning Map. As part of the update, an "IF" zoning district was
introduced; however, was not aligned with the property lines of the subject site. As a result, the
property was divided into two zones: the landlocked westerly portion designated IF, and the
easterly portion zoned M3.

On December 19, 2024, the City issued a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (TCO), allowing
the applicant to operate a vehicle towing/impounding lot only within the front (easterly) portion of
the subject site currently designated M3. The TCO was issued with the understanding the applicant
would submit a site plan for review and approval by staff soon after. The TCO is set to expire on
November 18, 2025. Pursuant to Table 11.21-4 (Commercial Industrial Zones Allowed Land Uses)
of SGMC Section 11.21.030 (Land Use Permission Tables), “vehicle towing/impounding” uses
are permitted by-right. The applicant is seeking to expand the business operations and occupy the
entire site; however, the rear portion must be re-zoned to M3 to allow the proposed operations.
Currently, the rear portion is cordoned off and only the front portion along Rayo Avenue is being
utilized for towing and impound operations.

ANALYSIS:

Zoning Map Amendment
The applicant is requesting to change the zoning of the rear portion of the property from IF to M3,
to match the current M3 zoning designation of the front portion of the property, with the intention
to expand the current vehicle towing and impound operations to the remainder of the site. If a zone
change is approved, a separate application for Design Review will be required prior to the approval
and completion of any site improvements necessary to accommodate the business expansion. The
Design Review process must be completed before the issuance of a business license or Certificate
of Occupancy for the expanded operations. Design Review is an administrative (staff level)
process that does not require a public hearing before the Planning Commission.

Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.22.060, the purpose of the IF zone is to continue the industrial job
base in the area, while allowing flexibility to incorporate a mix of uses and job options, supporting
innovative industry and living options in close proximity to transit, existing employment centers,
and major corridors. Furthermore, pursuant to SGMC Section 11.24.060, light and heavy
manufacturing (M2 and M3) zones are intended to implement the manufacturing/distribution place
type designation of the General Plan. These zones include uses such as industrial, manufacturing,
large-scale warehouse, distribution, or logistics facilities. The M3 zone provides dedicated
locations for the preservation and development of commercial and industrial activities.

The east and west block faces of Rayo Avenue, between Firestone Boulevard and Southern
Avenue, are currently designated M3 and predominantly occupied by industrial uses, with
exception to the LAUSD facility to the south of the project site at 5115 Southern Avenue, which
is designated IF. The front portion of the subject site, which abuts Rayo Avenue, is also designated
M3, aligning with the zoning of most properties along the street. Therefore, maintaining this M3
zoning designation is appropriate to ensure continued compatibility with existing and future

  11
 Planning Commission
(Zone Change PL25-146) – 9313 Rayo Ave.
May 20, 2025
Page 4 of 4

  industrial uses on adjacent properties. The rear portion of the site is designated IF and shares
  boundaries with other IF-designated parcels that front Atlantic Avenue. The proposed zone change
  for the rear portion of the site supports this zoning pattern and reinforces consistency along Atlantic
  Avenue. Furthermore, the change would facilitate future development that aligns with surrounding
  uses.

  Conclusion
  Based on the above analysis, staff has determined the proposed Zone Change will maintain
  consistency with the General Plan. The amendment supports the community's long-term vision by
  promoting orderly development, aligning land use designations with current needs, and ensuring
  compatibility with surrounding uses. Therefore, staff recommends approval of the Zone Change
  request.

  ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:

  The Planning Commission’s recommendation to the City Council for an amendment to the Zoning
  Map is not subject to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review because it is not an
  “approval” as defined in California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Section 15352, but rather a
  recommendation, and therefore does not commit the City to any definite course of action regarding
  the Zoning Code Amendment.

  RECOMMENDATION:

  Based on the evidence presented, Staff recommends that the Planning Commission consider:

  1. Adopting Resolution No. 2025-06 recommending City Council approve a request to change
  the zoning designation of a property at 9313 Rayo Avenue from IF (Industrial Flex) to M3
  (Heavy Manufacturing) and adopt an Ordinance, amending the citywide Zoning Map of Title
  11 (Zoning) of the SGMC.

  2. Finding that the recommendation to the City Council for an amendment to the Zoning Map is
  not subject to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review because it is not an
  “approval” as defined in California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Section 15352, but rather a
  recommendation, and therefore does not commit the City to any definite course of action
  regarding the Zoning Code Amendment.

  1.  Resolution No. 2025-06 and draft Ordinance
  2.  Applicant submittal including proposed zoning designation at 9313 Rayo Avenue

  4.  Draft Amended Zoning Map

SECTION 1. All of the facts set forth in the recitals are true and correct and are incorporated

SECTION 2. Based on substantial evidence, both written and oral, from the public hearing, the
Planning Commission makes the following findings:

  Zone Change

  A. The proposed zone change from IF (Industrial Flex) to M3 (Heavy Manufacturing)
  is appropriate based on the land use pattern of the surrounding area and the existing
  operations on the subject property. The zone change will eliminate the current split-
  zoning condition and apply a uniform zoning designation across the entire property.
  This action will clean up the zoning map to follow the actual property boundaries,
  promoting consistent and orderly land use regulation.

  B. The proposed zone change is consistent with the City of South Gate General Plan,
  including the policies and goals outlined in the Community Design Element. The
  property is located within the Rayo Industrial (Sub-area 2) District, which
  encourages heavy industrial uses. Aligning the entire parcel under the M3
  designation will support the intended industrial character of the area and ensure
  land use compatibility in accordance with the General Plan.

SECTION 3. The Planning Commission reviewed the project’s environmental impacts under the
California Environmental Quality Act (California Public Resources Code Section 21000, et seq.,
“CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 California Code of Regulations Section
15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”) and finds it is not an “approval” as defined in California
Code of Regulations, Title 14, Section 15352, but rather a recommendation, and therefore does
not commit the City to any definite course of action regarding the Zoning Code Amendment.

CALIFORNIA DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:
  SECTION 1. The City Council of the City of South Gate hereby approves a Zone Change
for the rear portion of the property located at 9313 Rayo Avenue (APNs: 6222-005-028 and 6222-
005-030), changing the zoning designation of the rear portion of the property from IF (Industrial
Flex) to M3 (Heavy Manufacturing), to match the current M3 zoning designation of the front
portion of the property. Accordingly, the Citywide Zoning Map of Title 11 (Zoning) of the South
Gate Municipal Code is hereby amended to reflect the revised zoning designation for the subject
property, as shown in the amended Zoning Map attached hereto as Exhibit “1” and incorporated
herein by this reference.
  SECTION 2. This Ordinance is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(“CEQA”) pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines because it can be seen with
certainty that there is no possibility the approval may have a significant effect on the environment.
The Zone Change consists of a map amendment to apply a uniform zoning designation to a
previously split-zoned parcel consistent with the General Plan and does not involve any new
development at this time.
  SECTION 3. If any Section, sentence, clause, or phrase of this Ordinance is for any reason
held to be invalid or unconstitutional by a decision of any court of any competent jurisdiction, such
decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of this ordinance. The City Council
hereby declares that it would have passed this Ordinance, and each and every Section, subsection,
sentence, clause and phrase thereof not declared invalid or unconstitutional without regard to
whether any portion of the ordinance would be subsequently declared invalid or unconstitutional.
  SECTION 4. The City Clerk shall certify the adoption of this Ordinance and shall cause
a copy of the same to be published in a manner prescribed by law.

  17
   SECTION 5. This Ordinance shall be in full force and effect thirty (30) days after its final
passage and adoption.
